name: Sweden
sources: GDP $261.5bn and population 8.56m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series SWE, 1990 (261,466,577,009 and 8,558,835). Same series as the rest of the roster - which makes Sweden, with a twentieth of the population of the United States, an eighth of Japan's, richer per head in 1990 than either.

Inflation 10.4%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, SWE 1990 = 10.367%. The highest in Western Europe outside Greece and Portugal, and the direct product of the credit-market deregulation of November 1985 feeding a property boom that broke in the autumn of 1990.

Policy rate 13.7%: three-month Swedish interbank rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 13.667% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TIB01SEM156N). The krona was unilaterally pegged to the ECU in May 1991 and the peg was defended in September 1992 with an overnight marginal rate of 500 per cent for six days before it broke on 19 November. The 13.7% here is the ordinary level before any of that; the model is not told the peg is coming.

Revenue 50% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Sweden 1990 = 49.5% - the highest in the OECD that year. This figure was checked against the OECD comparative table rather than recalled.

Gross public debt 40% of GDP: IMF Historical Public Debt Database, central government debt, SWE 1990 = 40.4%. CAVEAT: this is the CENTRAL government measure, not the general government measure used for most of this batch - the IMF WEO general-government series does not carry Sweden back to 1990. It is therefore a floor rather than a like-for-like figure, and the Swedish general-government number for 1990 is somewhat higher. Recorded here so the basis is visible rather than assumed.

Military 2.5% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), SWE 1990 = 2.462%. Armed neutrality is expensive; Sweden spent more of its output on defence in 1990 than Denmark, the Netherlands or Belgium, all of whom were in NATO.

Strength index 18: about 64,000 under arms at any moment but a war organisation of some 700,000 on mobilisation - roughly a tenth of the adult population - together with the only country of this size in the world building its own supersonic fighter (the Viggen in service, the Gripen in flight test), its own submarines and its own armour. Indexed above Spain's 16 and below Turkey's 24 on that basis: far fewer standing troops than either, far more industry behind them.

Gross fixed capital formation 28.8% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, SWE 1990 - a boom-top number, which is what it was. Split into public 3.4% and private 25.4% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual. CAVEAT: the total is transcribed; the public share is entered from reference knowledge of AMECO and is the softest number here.

Stability 76 and authoritarianism 0.08: below Germany's 80, above France's 75. Sweden had governed itself with remarkable placidity for fifty years, but on 15 February 1990 the Carlsson cabinet resigned outright when the Riksdag voted down its crisis package - a price and wage freeze with a two-year ban on strikes - and came back a week later having dropped the strike ban. A government falling over an incomes policy in the first six weeks of the game year is exactly the sort of thing this number should be able to see.

TFP trend 0.014: at France's 0.014. Swedish output fell in three consecutive years, 1991, 1992 and 1993, the worst peacetime contraction since the 1930s, and then produced one of the strongest productivity recoveries in the OECD on the back of telecommunications equipment. The average across the decade lands near the French rate by two very different routes.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.3723%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series SWE (Sweden): 8,336,605 in 1984 to 8,492,964 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 12 were held and are listed below with their citations; 36 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, comp_risc_superscalar, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> NOT HELD (semiconductors-computing said held, telecom-space said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space) matl_composite_structures -> HELD (aerospace-military said not held, materials-manufacturing said held; resolved to the board that owns the Materials domain, materials-manufacturing).

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 3 cells: bio_cross_sectional_imaging (health and agriculture board), bio_recombinant_pharma (health and agriculture board), core_pcr (health and agriculture board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

granted.source: Route (b), inherited from comp_microprocessor: World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 10.50 PCs per 100.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Hultman T, Stahl S, Hornes E, Uhlen M, 'Direct solid phase sequencing of genomic and plasmid DNA using magnetic beads as solid support', Nucleic Acids Research 1989;17(13):4937-46 (PMID 2668874), Department of Biochemistry and Biotechnology, Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm - a method that CAPTURES PCR PRODUCT on beads, so PCR is the assumed infrastructure rather than the subject. Corroborated by 'Alternative splicing of the platelet-derived growth factor A-chain transcript occurs in normal as well as tumor cells', Molecular and Cellular Biology 1989 (PMID 2779559), Department of Pathology, University Hospital, Uppsala. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 10.50 PCs per 100, 4.3x the World value of 2.45.
Oracle established a Swedish subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above). Sweden also holds comp_microprocessor at 10.50 PCs per 100.

Ericsson's AXE-10, the digital exchange system Sweden designed and exported, was in domestic service through the 1980s; R3 confirms independently - the Swedish NMT-450 network opened for service on 1 October 1981, the first NMT network anywhere, and World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 461,200 Swedish mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

The Swedish NMT network opened for service on 1 October 1981 - the first NMT network anywhere and the deployment this node's own source comment reads its floor from ('NMT in the Nordics from 1981'). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 461,200 Swedish mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990, the highest per head of any nation in this authored set.
Saab built the carbon-fibre wing and fin of the JAS 39 Gripen; the prototype first flew on 9 December 1988, before the start date.
ASEA's IRB 6 of 1974 was the first microprocessor-controlled all-electric industrial robot; the line was in series production at Vasteras and passed to ABB on the 1988 ASEA / Brown Boveri merger.

Ericsson PS-46/A pulse-Doppler look-down/shoot-down radar in the Saab JA 37 Viggen, in Flygvapnet service from 1980 — the first European pulse-Doppler fighter radar to enter service. Ericsson also produced the Giraffe pulse-Doppler ground radar from 1977 and went on to the PS-05/A for the Gripen.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2, and the earliest dated cell in this technology outside the United States: Degerblad M, Grunditz R, Hall K, Sjoeberg HE et al., 'Substitution therapy with recombinant growth hormone (somatrem) in adults with growth hormone deficiency', Acta Paediatrica Scandinavica Supplement 1987;337:170-1 (PMID 3481181), Department of Endocrinology, Karolinska Hospital, Stockholm - 1987, and note SUBSTITUTION THERAPY, which is limb A in one phrase. Corroborated by Albertsson-Wikland K, Aronson AS, Nilsson KO, Ritzen M, 'Recombinant somatropin in treatment of growth hormone deficient children in Sweden and Finland', Acta Paediatrica Scandinavica Supplement 1988;347:176-9 (PMID 3254032), Department of Paediatrics II, University of Gothenburg - a national treatment programme, not a single centre. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Sweden, 1990: 99% — the highest figure among the majors. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Sweden,SWE,1990,99').

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E1/E2, from the national diffusion history: US Congress Office of Technology Assessment, 'Health Care Technology and Its Assessment in Eight Countries' (OTA-BP-H-140, February 1995), chapter 7 'Health Care Technology in Sweden'. CT: the first head scanner was installed at the Karolinska Hospital, Stockholm, and 'by December 1978, Sweden had eight head scanners (all but one at regional hospitals) and six total body scanners (two of which were located at the largest central hospital)'; a 1985 Swedish consensus conference on stroke recommended that all hospitals should have CT scanners, and the chapter records that 'This report led to an increased diffusion of CT scanners in the late 1980s.' MRI: 'the first MRI scanner was introduced in Sweden in 1984 and installed in the Academic Hospital in Uppsala', and 'By 1990, however, the number of MRI units per population had caught up with the diffusion rate in most other European countries' (chapter table 7-6, sourced to Swedish Council on Technology Assessment in Health Care (SBU), 'MRI - Magnetic Resonance Imaging', English language summary, Stockholm 1992). LIMB C SEARCHED AND PARTLY FIRED, THEN CLEARED: there IS a named Swedish defeater candidate - after SPRI's 1984 assessment the Federation of County Councils adopted a moratorium on MRI - but the same source states it 'did not stop some hospitals from acquiring MRI' and that Sweden had caught up with the rest of Europe by 1990, so the defeater does not carry. LIMIT STATED: table 7-6's numeric columns are mangled in the scanned text and I did not transcribe them; this cell rests on the chapter's prose statements, which are unambiguous. Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half.
